difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.1.1 at source lines 124-134: for a morphism f in a category, four conditions are equivalent, namely being a monomorphism, having the diagonal map an isomorphism, having all sigma-type fibers mere propositions, and having a contractibility property. The author's proof (source lines 135-141) is a cycle of implications in which each step uses a different fact: the standard equivalence with the diagonal condition is quoted (line 136), conditions (1) and (3) are identified by reading injectivity as propositionality of the fibers of the map (f o blank) between sets (lines 137-138), condition (3) implies (4) because an inhabited mere proposition is contractible (line 139), and (4) implies (1) by exhibiting two elements of the contractible type and concluding equality (line 140). The statement is a four-way equivalence and records neither the fiber translation nor which of the four steps consumes contractibility.
